C005.subject: Long-term adherence to intermittent fasting
C005.object: long-term adherence to continuous calorie restriction among individuals with high baseline impulsivity
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Long-term adherence to intermittent fasting long-term adherence to continuous calorie restriction among individuals with high baseline impulsivity]

[PATH:empirical] Randomized controlled trial comparing 12-month adherence rates between intermittent fasting and continuous calorie restriction in adults with high trait impulsivity (measured via UPPS-P scale) — Directly tests the hypothesis by measuring actual adherence over the specified temporal scope and moderating variable.

[PATH:literature] Systematic review and meta-analysis of dietary adherence studies that include subgroup analyses by baseline impulsivity or self-regulation measures — Synthesizes existing evidence to identify whether impulsivity consistently moderates adherence differences between fasting and continuous restriction beyond 12 months.

[PATH:empirical] Longitudinal observational study using ecological momentary assessment to track real-time dietary decision-making and adherence in high-impulsivity individuals on intermittent vs. continuous restriction — Provides mechanistic insight into why impulsivity might differentially affect adherence, capturing day-to-day variability often missed in periodic self-reports.

scope.domain: adherence rates beyond 12 months, moderated by trait impulsivity

C006.subject: Long-term adherence to intermittent fasting
C006.object: long-term adherence to continuous calorie restriction
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Long-term adherence to intermittent fasting long-term adherence to continuous calorie restriction]

[PATH:literature] Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing adherence rates in intermittent fasting versus continuous calorie restriction at 12+ months — A comprehensive synthesis of existing RCT data would directly compare long-term adherence metrics (e.g., dropout rates, self-reported compliance) across both dietary approaches, providing empirical evidence to confirm or refute the hypothesis.

[PATH:empirical] Longitudinal cohort study using real-world dietary tracking apps (e.g., MyFitnessPal, Cronometer) to analyze sustained engagement with intermittent fasting vs. calorie restriction over >12 months — Observational data from large-scale user logs can reveal actual adherence patterns in naturalistic settings, complementing controlled trials and addressing potential biases in self-reported adherence.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical modeling of behavioral factors (e.g., habituation, dietary monotony, social constraints) that may differentially affect long-term adherence to intermittent fasting versus continuous calorie restriction — A formal model based on behavioral economics and psychological literature could generate testable predictions about adherence trajectories, guiding future empirical studies and clarifying mechanisms underlying any observed differences.

C007.subject: Intermittent fasting
C007.predicate: produces greater preservation of resting metabolic rate during weight loss compared to
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Intermittent fasting continuous calorie restriction]

[PATH:empirical] Controlled clinical trial comparing intermittent fasting (e.g., 16:8 or 5:2) with daily calorie restriction, measuring resting metabolic rate via indirect calorimetry at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months, with strict control for weight loss magnitude and physical activity. — Directly tests the hypothesis over the specified 12-month domain, providing causal evidence on RMR preservation differences.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of randomized trials on intermittent fasting versus continuous calorie restriction, focusing on resting metabolic rate outcomes at ≥12 months, with subgroup analyses for adherence and body composition changes. — Synthesizes existing evidence to increase statistical power and assess consistency across studies, addressing the disputed status of the hypothesis.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical modeling of adaptive thermogenesis under intermittent vs. continuous energy deficit, incorporating hormonal regulation (e.g., leptin, thyroid hormones) and metabolic adaptation dynamics. — Provides mechanistic insight into why RMR might be differentially preserved, guiding empirical predictions and interpretation of conflicting results.

scope.domain: resting metabolic rate change over 12 months

C008.subject: Intermittent fasting
C008.predicate: produces superior metabolic health benefits compared to
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Intermittent fasting continuous calorie restriction]

[PATH:empirical] Randomized controlled trial comparing time-restricted eating (16:8) vs. daily calorie restriction on insulin sensitivity and metabolic markers over 12 months in Western adults — Directly tests the hypothesis in the specified temporal and geographic scope, providing high-quality causal evidence on long-term metabolic adaptation.

[PATH:literature] Systematic review and meta-analysis of human studies on intermittent fasting vs. continuous calorie restriction, focusing on changes in resting metabolic rate and fat-free mass retention — Synthesizes existing evidence to assess whether intermittent fasting yields superior metabolic benefits, addressing the disputed status and clarifying effect consistency across populations.

[PATH:theoretical] Mechanistic study comparing the effects of intermittent fasting and continuous calorie restriction on circadian gene expression and mitochondrial efficiency in adipose tissue — Explores underlying biological pathways (e.g., autophagy, clock genes) that may explain differential long-term metabolic adaptations, helping to refute or confirm the hypothesis beyond correlational data.
